newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SLanka rupee ends flat on call rate, dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: SLanka rupee ends flat on call rate, dlr supply.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed flat against the dollar on Tuesday due to high call money rates and a high supply of dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.92 to the dollar, they said.
"There was a little demand for dollars, but the market was so well supplied that it made no difference and stayed near the Central Bank bottom," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by half a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.9050 and 60.0950.
Overnight call money rates closed at 16 percent after opening at 9.25 and rising to 17.5 percent, dealers said.
"Call rates soared because there was uncertainty in the value date in payment of a large inward remittance, which kept over four billion rupees out of cirulation," said a foreign bank dealer.

The National Development Bank Ltd recently sold 16.5 million shares for 260 rupees to foreign investors and raised over four billion rupees. Since the shares were part of the convertible debentures held by the government, the proceeds will go to the treasury, dealers said.
Dealers said the tight money situation was temporary and would ease once the transaction was completed.
